summary: Vacated an 1855 lighthouse reservation on a cluster of small islets in the Gulf of Mexico south of Marsh Island, Louisiana, and set them aside as Shell Keys Reservation, a reserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Revoked Executive Order 666, which had enlarged the Malate Barracks reservation in Manila.

Loosened a 1906 order on classified laborers so they could get pay raises, while still requiring a Civil Service Commission exam for promotion or transfer and capping pay at the usual rate for the job.
Added 372.45 acres of public land in Oklahoma Territory to the Fort Sill Military Reservation, withdrawing it from sale for military purposes.
Allowed four women, including two widows of War Department clerks, to be appointed to War Department clerical jobs without following the civil-service rules.
Amended the civil-service rules governing limits on transferring employees between positions.
Let Felix Neumann be appointed a clerk in the Smithsonian Institution's Bureau of International Exchanges without a civil-service examination.
Created the Tongass National Forest in the Territory of Alaska, reserving its timbered public lands from settlement, entry or sale while protecting valid existing rights.
Cut a strip of land reaching one mile back from the tide line on both sides of Valdez Arm out of the Chugach National Forest in Alaska.
Extended the protection of U.S. copyright law to citizens of Austria.

Rewrote the civil-service rule on transfers: employees generally needed three years in their current office and six months' service after absolute appointment, with the Commission able to waive some requirements.
Allowed Rachel F. Sullivan to be reinstated as a clerk in the Boston post office despite the time limit in the reinstatement rule.
Brought R. D. Scarlett and John M. Newton, clothing examiners for the Army quartermaster's department in Philadelphia since 1904, into the classified civil service.
Reserved land in Alabama for the War Department's use in improving the Black Warrior River.
Redrew the boundaries of Camp Keithley, a military reservation on Lake Lanao in Mindanao first reserved in 1905 as Camp Marahui, covering about 17,076 acres.
Removed certain lands in Wyoming from the Medicine Bow National Forest, restoring lands not otherwise reserved to the public domain.

Directed the U.S. Civil Service Commission and federal workers in Porto Rico to help the island's new civil service commission, and allowed transfers from Porto Rico's civil service into the federal service.
Allowed Charles M. Irelan to move from the Patent Office to a War Department clerical job without waiting out the six-month limit on transfers after reinstatement.
Let bank examiner Charles E. Knight be appointed shipping commissioner at the port of San Francisco without a civil-service exam, since no list of eligible candidates existed.
Allowed William Stimpel to be appointed disciplinarian at the Carlisle Indian School in Pennsylvania after a noncompetitive exam showing his experience.
Set the consular fee for issuing or extending a passport at $1.00.
Set aside Three Arch Rocks, a group of small islands off the Oregon coast, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds and animals.
Let automatic scale mechanician John V. Davis stay on the job until his current assignment was finished, without meeting civil-service rules.
Partly revoked an 1853 order that had reserved land at Rock Harbor on Isle Royale in Lake Superior, Michigan.
Reserved tracts of public land in Alaska, including sites at Donnelly's, McCallum's and Paxson's roadhouses plus a right of way, for the Army Signal Corps to run its military telegraph lines.
Set aside the small islands off the Washington coast between set latitudes, including Flattery Rocks, Ozette Island and White Rock, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds and animals.
Created Copalis Rock Reservation from small islands off the Washington coast, including Arch Island, Sea Lion Rock and Copalis Rock, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds and animals.

Reserved the small islands off the Washington coast between set latitudes, among them Carroll Islets, James Island and Quillayute Needles, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds and animals.
Named Thursday, November 28, 1907, as a national day of thanksgiving, noting a year free from famine, pestilence and war.
Added timbered lands in California to the Lassen Peak National Forest.
Enlarged the Stanislaus National Forest in California with additional lands partly covered with timber.
Set apart the San Benito National Forest from timbered public lands in California, reserving them from settlement or entry.
Authorized the appointment of retired Revenue-Cutter Service captain Charles H. McLellan, an expert on lifeboats, to keep superintending lifesaving-equipment construction without civil-service rules.
Allowed John P. Scruggs, removed as a South Carolina deputy revenue collector on misconduct charges later found largely unfounded, to be reappointed without civil-service rules.
Released post cemetery lands at Fort Sumner that had been reserved by an 1871 executive order.
Withdrew a large tract in the Territories of Arizona and New Mexico from sale and settlement and added it to the Navajo Reservation, protecting valid existing rights.
Let Joseph B. Dalton be appointed a skilled laborer in the Bureau of the Census without a civil-service exam.
Set apart additional lands in New Mexico for the Indians of the Jicarilla Indian Reservation, withdrawing them from sale and settlement.
Declared Oklahoma admitted as a state after voters ratified the constitution drafted under the 1906 enabling act for Oklahoma and Indian Territories.
Created the Gila Cliff-Dwellings National Monument to protect the cliff houses in the Mogollon Mountains of New Mexico Territory, inside the Gila National Forest.
Gave Marine Corps signalmen the same extra pay that Navy signalmen received.
Allowed carriage drivers for the President, department heads and the Secretary to the President to be hired without civil-service rules or labor regulations.

Allowed the Civil Service Commission, in any district, to certify the three highest qualified candidates from its register when filling unskilled laborer jobs in federal offices outside Washington, D.C.
Gave the Civil Service Commission discretion to waive exams for permitted transfers and promotions and substitute other tests of fitness, with reasons recorded in its minutes.
Added timbered lands in the Territory of Arizona to the Prescott National Forest.
Adjusted the rules for extra pay given to Navy gun pointers.
Announced a commercial agreement with Great Britain lowering U.S. duties on British paintings, drawings and statuary to 15 percent, in return for free entry of American commercial travelers' samples.
Gave employees of the Geological Survey's technologic branch the rights of examined civil servants, except that they could not transfer outside that branch.
Reserved East Timbalier Island, a small marshy island in the Gulf of Mexico off Louisiana and once part of a military reservation, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Enlarged the Monticello National Forest in Utah with additional timbered lands.
Established the Vegas National Forest on timbered public lands in Nevada, reserving them from settlement or entry.
Added timbered lands in Utah to the Aquarius National Forest.
Allowed William McCambridge of Illinois to move from the excepted to the competitive class at the Interstate Commerce Commission without an exam.
Designated Charles Earl, solicitor of the Department of Commerce and Labor, to serve as acting Secretary of the Interior while the Secretary and Assistant Secretary were away.

Told federal record keepers to give credentialed agents of the Carnegie Institution of Washington's Department of Historical Research access to departmental archives for historical research when convenient.
Allowed Emily G. Stickney's temporary job as clerk examiner in the Bureau of Chemistry to be extended until an appointment could be made from a January 1908 exam.
Directed the Civil Service Commission, at any member of Congress's request, to help test applicants for appointment to the U.S. Military and Naval academies, if no added expense resulted.
Set apart the Arkansas National Forest from timbered public lands in Arkansas, reserving them from settlement or entry.
Created Tonto National Monument to protect two prehistoric cliff-dwelling ruins in Gila County, Arizona, about two miles south of the Salt River Reservoir, along with one section of land.
Added timbered lands in California to the San Gabriel National Forest.
Set apart the Verde National Forest from timbered public lands in the Territory of Arizona.
Amended the 1897 diplomatic instructions and 1896 consular regulations to define the relative rank of diplomatic officers.

Reorganized the Isthmian Canal Commission, setting a quorum, assigning its duties under the Secretary of War, and having the Chairman, also Chief Engineer, divide the work into departments such as construction, civil administration, law and sanitation.
Amended the civil-service rules to allow appointment of shipping commissioners at certain ports; later revoked by Executive Order 733.
Enlarged the San Bernardino National Forest in California with additional timbered lands.
Let 15 irregular employees working under irrigation engineers in the Indian service stay on temporarily without civil-service rules, but barred adding to the force or transferring them.
Allowed 126 irregular employees of the Union Agency to remain temporarily without civil-service exams, while barring new additions to the force or transfers out of the agency.
Removed certain lands in Oregon from the Blue Mountains National Forest and set terms for restoring them to homestead settlement.
Added timbered lands in California to the Monterey National Forest.
Accepted land in Marin County, California, donated by William Kent and Elizabeth Thatcher Kent, and set it aside as Muir Woods National Monument.

Added misdemeanors to the Canal Zone penal code for vagrancy, begging, loitering around canal camps and buildings, public drunkenness and disorderly conduct, punishable by up to $25 or 30 days in jail.
Allowed common carriers in the Canal Zone to auction freight, baggage or other property left unclaimed for six months with unpaid charges, after advertising the sale.
Divided the Canal Zone into three judicial circuits built from the administrative districts of Ancon, Emperador and Gorgona, and Cristobal.

Extended a 1904 Republic of Panama law excluding certain aliens to the Canal Zone, with fines for companies or individuals who let such travelers escape into the Zone, exempting workers brought in for canal construction.
Proclaimed the Grand Canyon of the Colorado River, described as the greatest eroded canyon in the United States, a national monument within the Grand Canyon National Forest in Arizona Territory.
Enlarged the Tonto National Forest in Arizona Territory with additional timbered lands and folded in the former Pinal Mountains National Forest.
Excepted from examination shipping commissioners in the Department of Commerce and Labor who earned $2,500 or more in fiscal year 1907.
Allowed Ernest Coldwell, whose job as a Tennessee internal-revenue collector ended when two districts merged, to be appointed a revenue agent without civil-service rules.
Abolished the Huron land district in South Dakota and transferred it to the Pierre land district.
Moved certain lands from the Colfax land district in New Mexico into the Lincoln land district.
Reserved a tract on the Tanana River at Minto, Alaska, as a military reservation for the Army Signal Corps to operate telegraph lines.
Allowed James S. Wickham to work in the Bureau of the Census on experimental tabulating machinery without a civil-service exam.
Allowed Indians to be appointed messengers in the Office of Indian Affairs after a noncompetitive exam; later revoked by Executive Order 754.
Rewrote Civil Service Rule VII on how competitive positions are filled, with the Commission certifying enough names from the top of the register for appointing officers to consider three per vacancy.
Rewrote the civil-service rule on temporary appointments, allowing them only when the public interest required, with prior Commission approval, and only until eligibles could be certified.
Created Pinnacles National Monument to protect the Pinnacles Rocks and the caves beneath them, inside the Pinnacles National Forest in California.
Announced a new trade agreement with France applying lower U.S. duty rates to champagne and other sparkling wines starting February 1, 1908, in return for French concessions on American products.
Set monthly pay for Navy mess attendants who were U.S. citizens at $30, $25 and $20 by class, and gave certified stewards and cooks $5 a month extra.
Rewrote the boundary of the November 1907 addition to the Jicarilla Indian Reservation in New Mexico to fix a conflict with the Navajo Reservation addition.
Revised the boundary of the November 1907 Navajo Reservation addition in Arizona and New Mexico to resolve its overlap with the Jicarilla Indian Reservation addition.
Reserved described lands in Alabama for the War Department's work improving the Black Warrior, Warrior and Tombigbee rivers.
Enlarged the Trinity National Forest in California with additional timbered lands.
Abolished the Woodward land district in Oklahoma and moved its lands, business and records to the Alva land district.
Allowed Isabel E. McKinley to be reinstated in the War Department regardless of how long she had been gone.
Revised the civil-service exceptions for the mint and assay service so each mint or assay office could have one private secretary or confidential clerk and one cashier without examination.
